phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve
one more problem.
Now, in this problem, we are given that the boat covers
sixty kilometer downstream in three hours,
and the same sixty kilometer upstream in five hours.
The question is
asking us to find the speed of the boat
in still water.
Let the speed of the boat in still water be b kilometer per hour,
and let the speed of the current be c kilometer per hour.
Now, let us understand downstream and upstream.
When the boat moves along with the current,
the current helps the boat move faster.
So downstream speed equals b plus c.
When the boat moves against the current,
the current slows the boat down.
So upstream speed equals b minus c. Now, the important point is we are not given the speeds directly.
We are given distance and time. So first, we need to find both speeds using the formula,
speed equals distance divided by time.
For downstream,
sixty divided by three gives twenty.
So downstream speed b plus c equals twenty.
Now, let us find the upstream speed. Sixty divided by five gives twelve.
So upstream speed
b minus c equals twelve. Done.
Now, the remaining part is easy.
If we add both equations, c gets canceled.
After simplifying, two b equals thirty-two, so b equals sixteen.
Hence,
the speed of the boat in still water is sixteen kilometer per hour.
So the correct option is option A.
